analysis.title: DeskTalk - Fedspeak has entered the chat
key_insights: OIS markets imply up to 3x25bp (or 1x50bp and 1x25bp) of Fed hikes left in this cycle after Waller's remarks combined with a strong CPI print.
Pricing for the December meeting rose to 28bp of hikes from 21bp before Waller spoke.
Citi thinks the bar for a 50bp hike is high and sees hikes being pushed into 2027.
FOMC members appear to be telegraphing a more hawkish reaction function than markets expected.
Logan said it would make sense to pause after two more increases, which is conservative relative to market pricing.
Schmid described the current policy rate as fairly accommodative. Goolsbee called the October CPI report 'borderline disturbing'.
Bowman, previously very dovish, said there is still work to do. Paulson implicitly pushed back, saying gradual tightening seems appropriate.

Governor Warsh prefers limited forward guidance, in contrast to the other members' vocal stance. Citi's trader speculates a shift in the political environment after the midterms may have prompted the change while inflation data stays hot.
Warsh gives opening remarks Monday at the Productivity and Jobs Task Force Conference. It is unclear whether he will address monetary policy.

Citi will watch upcoming Fedspeak from Hammack, Schmid, Williams, Collins and Daly ahead of Friday's PPI. Surprise media appearances are possible (Kashkari perhaps). Williams could be more indicative of the dovish/centrist contingent.
